instruction: For maximum privacy, I'd like Chrome to automatically clear cookies and site data whenever I close the browser. Can you enable this setting?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"profile":{"exit_type":1,"content_settings":{"exceptions":{"cookies":{}}}}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable Chrome's 'Clear cookies and site data when you quit Chrome' setting. The evaluator checks profile.exit_type and content_settings.exceptions.cookies for session-only settings in Chrome Preferences. Initial state: exit_type=1 (continue where left off), no session-only cookies. Expected state: either exit_type=4 or session-only cookie setting (setting==1) enabled. Note: This specifically checks cookies/site data clearing, not comprehensive browsing data (history, cache, downloads) clearing, as Chrome's feature from the source URL is limited to cookies and site data.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly checks Chrome's 'Clear cookies and site data when you quit Chrome' setting by examining both exit_type==4 and session-only cookie settings (setting==1 in content_settings.exceptions.cookies)

Instruction explicitly asks to 'clear cookies and site data' which matches Chrome's actual feature (from source URL https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/2392709), not comprehensive browsing data clearing
Coverage is complete: The getter checks both mechanisms Chrome uses for this setting (exit_type and session-only cookies)
Metric logic is correct: exact_match properly compares result 'true' with expected 'true'
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are read in saved state, not in-memory state
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true' represents the enabled state of the setting
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts Chrome preference state → returns 'true'/'false' → exact_match compares with expected 'true'
